spec.scope: Build a REST API for personal notes using Node.js and Express. It features three endpoints allowing users to create a note, list all notes, and delete a note by id. Notes are stored in-memory with a JavaScript object, requiring no external database or authentication mechanisms.

decisions.decision: Use a JavaScript object for in-memory storage of notes.
decisions.rationale: Simplifies implementation and matches the lightweight requirement given the constraint of no external databases.

decisions.decision: Endpoints will be mounted at the root level with specific paths: POST /notes, GET /notes, and DELETE /notes/:id.
decisions.rationale: This provides direct and unambiguous access paths as per requirements.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /notes accepts JSON payload with fields { "title": "string", "body": "string", "category": "string", "tags": ["string"] }. On success, the response is { "id": <sequential integer>, "title": "...", "body": "...", "category": "...", "tags": [...] }. On error, return { "error": { "message": "..." } }.
GET /notes returns all notes in an array of JSON objects with fields { "id": <integer>, "title": "...", "body": "...", "category": "...", "tags": [...] }.
DELETE /notes/:id removes the note with the specified integer id. On success, return 200. If id does not exist, return 404 with { "error": { "message": "Note not found" } }.
The auto-generated id for each note is a sequential integer starting at 1.

files_to_create.purpose: Creates and configures the Express application, mounts all routes, and starts listening on a specified port.
Defines Express routes and handlers for POST /notes, GET /notes, and DELETE /notes/:id.
Implements the in-memory storage logic for storing, retrieving, and deleting notes.

out_of_scope: Any form of persistent storage beyond in-memory solutions.
Client-side application views or front-end components.
